title_en: Fan Youfu v. Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Branch — retrial of dispute over futures trading contract
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading, a futures company must satisfy three prerequisites before taking forced liquidation measures: first, the client's margin is insufficient; second, the client fails to timely add margin as required; and third, the client fails to timely close positions on their own. If a futures company carries out forced liquidation in violation of the above provisions and contractual agreements, causing losses to the client, it shall bear corresponding liability in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Fan Youfu v. Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Business Department — retrial of dispute over futures trading contract

【Ruling Summary】

In accordance with the provisions of Article 38(2) of the Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading, a futures company must satisfy three preconditions before taking a forced liquidation measure: first, the client's margin is insufficient; second, the client fails to promptly add margin as required; and third, the client fails to promptly close positions on its own. If a futures company causes damage to the client as a result of forced liquidation in violation of the foregoing provisions and the contract, it shall bear corresponding liability in accordance with law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 111

Petitioner (defendant at first instance, appellant in second instance): Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Business Department. Domicile: No. 314 Xinhua Road, Heping District, Tianjin.

Responsible person: Han Bing, manager of the department.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xuehui, lawyer of Beijing Zhongtian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhan Min, lawyer of Beijing Zhongzi Law Firm.

Respondent (plaintiff at first instance, appellee in second instance): Fan Youfu, male, born July 15, 1960, Han ethnicity, unemployed, residing at No. 15, West 3rd Lane, Xinsheng Street, Area 19, Fanzhuang Village, Huaming Town, Dongli District, Tianjin.

Agent ad litem: Li Ling, lawyer of Beijing Hantao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shen Li, lawyer of Beijing Hantao Law Firm.

The petitioner, Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Business Department), dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2009) Jin Gao Min Er Zhong Zi No. 0028 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court in the dispute over a futures trading contract with Fan Youfu, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court decided to grant the retrial by Civil Ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 147 and formed a collegial panel composed of Jia Wei as presiding judge, and acting judges Sha Ling and Zhou Lunjun as members to conduct the trial, with Zhao Suijun serving as clerk. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On April 7, 2008, Fan Youfu filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court, alleging that, in accordance with the contract and the provisions of the Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading, the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department had damaged his rights and interests. He requested the court to order the Tianjin Business Department to compensate him for losses of RMB 9,027,085.66 and bear the litigation costs.

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court found at first instance:

On March 5, 2007, Fan Youfu and the Tianjin Business Department entered into a futures brokerage contract and two supplementary agreements (supplements 1 and 2), entrusting the Tianjin Business Department to conduct futures trading for Fan Youfu in accordance with trading instructions. Article 6 of the contract stipulated: "The Tianjin Business Department has the right to adjust the margin ratio on its own at any time in accordance with the provisions of the futures exchange or market conditions. The adjustment of margin by the Tianjin Business Department shall be subject to the announcement or adjustment notice issued by the Tianjin Business Department." Article 7 stipulated: "The Tianjin Business Department has the right to increase the margin ratio for Fan Youfu individually at any time based on its own judgment. In such circumstances, the notice of increase in margin shall be issued separately to Fan Youfu." Article 8 stipulated: "Before placing a new trading instruction or during the course of holding positions, Fan Youfu shall at all times monitor his positions, margin and equity changes." Article 10 stipulated: "If, due to trading losses or other reasons, the risk ratio of Fan Youfu falls below 100%, the Tianjin Business Department shall stop accepting any opening instructions from Fan Youfu and shall issue a margin call notice to Fan Youfu in the manner agreed in this contract. Fan Youfu shall promptly add margin or immediately take measures to reduce positions before the opening of the next trading day; otherwise, the Tianjin Business Department has the right, without prior notice to Fan Youfu, to forcibly liquidate part or all of Fan Youfu's open positions, up to the extent that Fan Youfu's risk ratio exceeds 100%. Fan Youfu shall bear the handling fees for forced liquidation and any losses arising therefrom." Article 11 stipulated: "If Fan Youfu is unable to promptly add margin, he shall take measures to reduce positions on his own to meet the margin requirements of the Tianjin Business Department, and shall avoid being subject to forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department as far as possible. Fan Youfu shall not claim rights from the Tianjin Business Department on the grounds that the timing, price or quantity of forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department is unfavorable." Article 14 stipulated: "The Tianjin Business Department shall issue daily trading settlement statements, margin adjustment notices, margin call notices and other notifications to Fan Youfu after the close of each trading day..."

After the contract was signed, prior to December 24, 2007, Fan Youfu held 33 lots of the Cu0802 contract, 369 lots of the Cu0803 contract, and 10 lots of the Cu0804 contract. On December 24, 2007, in accordance with the notice from the Tianjin Business Department, Fan Youfu voluntarily closed 270 lots of soybean positions, meeting the margin level required by the Tianjin Business Department. After the market closed at 15:00, at 18:50, the Tianjin Business Department notified Fan Youfu to add margin. Fan Youfu deposited margin of RMB 1.5 million at 13:48 on December 25, 2007. At 08:59 on December 25, 2007, during the opening call auction, the Tianjin Business Department forcibly liquidated 412 lots of short positions held by Fan Youfu, with the following liquidation prices: 33 lots of Cu0802 at RMB 62,390/ton, 369 lots of Cu0803 at RMB 61,250/ton, and 10 lots of Cu0804 at RMB 60,840/ton. On that day, the closing prices were: Cu0802 at RMB 58,850/ton, Cu0803 at RMB 57,970/ton, and Cu0804 at RMB 58,050/ton. Calculated based on the difference between the forced liquidation price and the closing price on that day, the loss on 33 lots of Cu0802 was RMB 471,900, on 369 lots of Cu0803 was RMB 6,051,600, and on 10 lots of Cu0804 was RMB 139,500, totaling RMB 6,663,000.

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court held that the futures brokerage contract and supplementary agreements signed on March 5, 2007 between Fan Youfu and the Tianjin Business Department did not violate any relevant laws and regulations, were legally valid, and both parties should fully perform their rights and obligations under the contract. Futures trading involves high risks. In this case, as a client of the Tianjin Business Department for futures trading, Fan Youfu had been warned of the risks in both the Account Opening Application Form and the Risk Disclosure Statement for Futures Trading, confirmed by his signature. Meanwhile, Article 3 of the futures brokerage contract also contained clear provisions regarding the risks that might arise during trading and their consequences. As a trading client, Fan Youfu should, during the holding of positions, at all times monitor changes in his margin and equity, and when foreseeing that increased risks might lead to forced liquidation, should proactively add margin or voluntarily reduce positions to avoid losses. Therefore, Fan Youfu should bear corresponding liability. As the trading venue, the Tianjin Business Department had a duty to supervise the futures market risks, and should warn clients of risks that might arise or had already arisen and notify clients to add margin within a reasonable time. In this case, although the Tianjin Business Department issued a margin call notice to Fan Youfu in accordance with the relevant provisions on futures trading and the agreement of the parties, it failed to provide Fan Youfu with a reasonable time to add margin, thereby causing the losses from the forced liquidation. Accordingly, the Tianjin Business Department should bear corresponding compensation liability. Fan Youfu's actual losses should be based on the price differences between the forced liquidation prices and the closing prices on that day: RMB 471,900 for 33 lots of Cu0802, RMB 6,051,600 for 369 lots of Cu0803, and RMB 139,500 for 10 lots of Cu0804, totaling RMB 6,663,000. Fan Youfu's claim for losses of RMB 9,027,085.66 based on the lowest price on December 28, 2007 lacked a sufficient factual basis. The Tianjin Business Department's defense that the forced liquidation was in compliance with relevant laws and that it should not compensate Fan Youfu for economic losses lacked legal basis and was not supported. Accordingly, both parties should jointly bear responsibility for the losses caused to Fan Youfu. In summary, the court, in accordance with Article 120 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 39 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Futures Disputes, ruled: 1. The Tianjin Business Department shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Fan Youfu for 60% of his economic loss of RMB 6,663,000, i.e., RMB 3,997,800. 2. Fan Youfu's other claims were rejected. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,989 was to be borne by Fan Youfu in the amount of RMB 44,993.4 and by the Tianjin Business Department in the amount of RMB 29,995.6.

Both the Tianjin Business Department and Fan Youfu were dissatisfied with the first instance judgment of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court and filed appeals with the Tianjin High People's Court. Fan Youfu appealed, alleging: The first instance judgment had unclear factual findings and improper allocation of liability, and should be amended according to law. 1. The first instance judgment had unclear factual findings. (1) Existing evidence fully proved that at approximately 2:00 p.m. on December 24, 2007, Wang Jianling, manager of the Tianjin Business Department, notified Fan Youfu orally and in writing that, due to insufficient margin, he needed to add margin or voluntarily close 65 lots of copper contracts. Fan Youfu immediately took voluntary closing measures by placing orders to close 65 lots of copper contracts, but the Tianjin Business Department also duplicated the orders and placed another 65 lots of copper contracts on its own, totaling 130 lots. Due to market conditions, the orders were not executed. Fan Youfu then, as required by the Tianjin Business Department, voluntarily closed 270 lots of soybean contracts, meeting the margin level required by the Tianjin Business Department. Meanwhile, in accordance with the contract, Fan Youfu attempted to pay margin to the Tianjin Business Department by check, but such payment was refused. (2) The first instance judgment stated that Fan Youfu deposited margin of RMB 1.5 million at 13:48 on December 25, 2007, which was inconsistent with the facts. At approximately 9:00 a.m. on December 25, 2007, Fan Youfu provided his bank fund card, with funds immediately available, to the Tianjin Business Department as per usual practice for margin payment, but the Tianjin Business Department delayed the transfer to its own account until the afternoon. In reality, Fan Youfu had paid the margin at approximately 9:00 a.m. (3) The Tianjin Business Department failed to consistently notify Fan Youfu to add margin in the manner and time required by Article 10 of the contract. On the 24th, the manager Wang Jianling notified Fan Youfu orally and in writing, but after the second increase in the margin ratio, the subsequent margin call notice was neither reasonable in time nor seriously violated the contract. (4) The first instance judgment had errors in the calculation of losses and allocation of liability. 2. The first instance judgment had improper allocation of liability. It ruled that the Tianjin Business Department bore 60% liability and Fan Youfu bore 40% liability, which was indeed improper. This case arose because the Tianjin Business Department seriously breached the contract and willfully infringed Fan Youfu's rights to add margin and voluntarily close positions. Fan Youfu paid margin and took measures to reduce positions in accordance with the contract, but the Tianjin Business Department abused its forced liquidation power. According to law, the Tianjin Business Department should bear full liability, i.e., compensate Fan Youfu for economic losses of RMB 9,027,085.66. During the second instance proceedings, Fan Youfu further amended his claim to request the court to order the Tianjin Business Department to compensate him for liquidation losses of RMB 13,066,500. Fan Youfu requested: 1. Set aside the first instance judgment and amend it to order the Tianjin Business Department to compensate Fan Youfu for economic losses of RMB 9,027,085.66; 2. The first and second instance case acceptance fees shall be borne by the Tianjin Business Department. In response to Fan Youfu's grounds of appeal and claims, the Tianjin Business Department defended: The forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department was in compliance with the contract between the parties. Because at the close on December 24, 2007, the copper contracts held by Fan Youfu had a price limit up, and market conditions changed, causing Fan Youfu's margin to be insufficient. Since the company only allowed margin payments from registered settlement accounts, Fan Youfu submitted a check from his unit on the 25th to pay margin, which was refused. Therefore, the losses in Fan Youfu's account should be borne by himself.

The Tianjin Business Department appealed, alleging: The court of first instance recognized that the Futures Brokerage Contract and supplementary agreements signed by both parties were legally valid. Article 10 of the Futures Brokerage Contract provided: If, due to trading losses or other reasons, the risk ratio of Fan Youfu falls below 100%, the Tianjin Business Department shall stop accepting any opening instructions from Fan Youfu and shall issue a margin call notice to Fan Youfu in the manner agreed in this contract. Fan Youfu shall promptly add margin or immediately take measures to reduce positions before the opening of the next trading day; otherwise, the Tianjin Business Department has the right, without prior notice to Fan Youfu, to forcibly liquidate part or all of Fan Youfu's open positions, up to the extent that Fan Youfu's risk ratio exceeds 100%. Fan Youfu shall bear the handling fees for forced liquidation and any losses arising therefrom. Article 36(2) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Futures Disputes provides: "If the client's trading margin is insufficient and the client fails to add margin within the time limit stipulated in the futures brokerage contract, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the futures brokerage contract; if the provisions are not clear, the futures company has the right to forcibly liquidate the client's open positions, and the losses caused by the forced liquidation shall be borne by the client." In this case, the forced liquidation carried out by the Tianjin Business Department against Fan Youfu was fully in compliance with the above contractual provisions and judicial interpretations. Therefore, the forced liquidation should be lawful and valid, and the losses resulting therefrom should be borne by Fan Youfu. Secondly, the losses in Fan Youfu's account were caused by his incorrect trading direction and inability to add margin in time, encountering market risks, not by the Tianjin Business Department's failure to provide a reasonable time for margin addition. After the close on December 24, 2007, the Tianjin Business Department issued a forced liquidation notice to Fan Youfu, requiring him to add margin of RMB 13.36 million before the opening of the next trading day; otherwise, all or part of Fan Youfu's positions would be liquidated. If Fan Youfu had added the funds before or around 9:30 on the 25th, and the Tianjin Business Department had already forcibly liquidated his positions before that time, then Fan Youfu could argue that the Tianjin Business Department did not provide him with a reasonable time to add margin. However, the fact is that on December 25, Fan Youfu was unable to add the margin required by the Tianjin Business Department, and did not deposit RMB 1.5 million until 13:48 in the afternoon. The time and amount of the deposit were far from what was required in the Tianjin Business Department's margin call notice. Therefore, the losses in Fan Youfu's account had nothing to do with whether the Tianjin Business Department provided a reasonable time to add margin. In summary, the first instance judgment was erroneous in its factual findings and application of law and should be set aside. The Tianjin Business Department requested: Set aside the first instance judgment and amend it to reject Fan Youfu's claims. In response to the Tianjin Business Department's grounds of appeal and claims, Fan Youfu argued: The Tianjin Business Department's grounds of appeal were untenable and its appeal should be dismissed. The Tianjin Business Department unilaterally and substantially increased the margin ratio and, contrary to normal practice, forcibly liquidated 412 lots of copper contracts. It should bear full compensation liability for Fan Youfu's losses.

In addition to confirming the facts found at first instance, the Tianjin High People's Court further found: On December 25, 2007, the Tianjin Business Department increased the margin ratio to 16.5%. The transaction records in the Trading Settlement Statement issued by the Tianjin Business Department to Fan Youfu for December 25, 2007, showed a realized profit and loss on liquidation of RMB -13,066,500.

The Tianjin High People's Court held in the second instance that the issues in dispute were whether the Tianjin Business Department should bear compensation liability for the losses caused to Fan Youfu by the forced liquidation, and what kind of compensation liability; and what standard should be used to calculate the losses from forced liquidation.

Regarding whether the Tianjin Business Department should bear compensation liability for the losses caused to Fan Youfu by the forced liquidation and what kind of compensation liability: The court held that the margin system is an important part of risk control in futures trading and a prerequisite for the stability and healthy development of the futures market. The amount of margin is adjusted by futures trading regulatory bodies in accordance with the actual conditions of futures trading. However, a futures exchange or futures company should give a client a reasonable time to add margin. In this case, after the close at 15:00 on December 24, 2007, the Tianjin Business Department notified Fan Youfu at 18:50 to add margin of RMB 13.36 million. At 08:59 on December 25, 2007, during the opening call auction, the Tianjin Business Department forcibly liquidated 412 lots of copper contracts held by Fan Youfu. This act turned Fan Youfu's unrealized losses into realized losses, and during that period, Fan Youfu had no way to deliver the margin to the Tianjin Business Department's account. In particular, on December 24, 2007, Fan Youfu had voluntarily closed positions as required by the Tianjin Business Department and had already reached the margin level required by the Tianjin Business Department, fulfilling his duty of care. At 18:50 after the close on the same day, the futures company substantially increased the margin ratio to 16.5%. Regarding this sudden change, the Tianjin Business Department did not give Fan Youfu any special notice, thereby causing Fan Youfu to lose a reasonable expectation of the amount of margin to be added. To protect the interests of the client, the losses caused thereby should be borne by the Tianjin Business Department. Although Article 10 of the futures brokerage contract and supplementary agreements provided: If, due to trading losses or other reasons, the risk ratio of Fan Youfu falls below 100%, the Tianjin Business Department shall issue a margin call notice to Fan Youfu in the manner agreed in the contract. Fan Youfu shall promptly add margin or immediately take measures to reduce positions before the opening of the next trading day; otherwise, the Tianjin Business Department has the right, without prior notice to Fan Youfu, to forcibly liquidate part or all of Fan Youfu's open positions, up to the extent that Fan Youfu's risk ratio exceeds 100%. Fan Youfu shall bear the handling fees for forced liquidation and any losses arising therefrom. However, the above contract did not stipulate a reasonable time for adding margin. The Tianjin Business Department placed orders for forced liquidation before the banks had opened for business, which clearly failed to give Fan Youfu a reasonable time to add margin. Fan Youfu was not at fault in this regard. The forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department had a direct causal relationship with Fan Youfu's losses, and it should bear corresponding compensation liability. Regarding the Tianjin Business Department's argument that Fan Youfu did not add funds before or around 9:30 on December 25, 2007, and did not deposit RMB 1.5 million until 13:48 in the afternoon, and that the time and amount of the deposit were far from what was required in the margin call notice, so the losses in Fan Youfu's account had nothing to do with whether the Tianjin Business Department provided a reasonable time to add margin: because the Tianjin Business Department had already placed orders to forcibly liquidate Fan Youfu's 412 lots of copper contracts before the opening of the futures market on December 25, 2007, and the corresponding losses had already occurred, whether Fan Youfu added margin thereafter had no legal causal relationship with those losses. The court therefore did not support the Tianjin Business Department's argument.

Regarding the issue of the standard for calculating losses from forced liquidation. There is no relevant provision in China's laws or administrative regulations on the calculation standard for forced liquidation losses. According to the content reflected in the "Transaction Settlement Statement" for Fan Youfu dated December 25, 2007, issued by the Tianjin Business Department to Fan Youfu, the amount of RMB 9,027,085.66 claimed by Fan Youfu in the first-instance lawsuit is indeed a forced liquidation loss and should be upheld. In summary, the facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear, but the application of law was improper and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled as follows: 1. Revoke the Civil Judgment (2008) Yi Zhong Min Er Chu Zi No. 61 of the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court; 2. The Tianjin Business Department shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Fan Youfu for economic losses of RMB 9,027,085.66. If the monetary payment obligation is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,989 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,990 shall be borne by the Tianjin Business Department.

The Tianjin Business Department, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment of the Tianjin High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) The second-instance judgment erred in applying the law. The second-instance judgment held that the Tianjin Business Department should give the client a reasonable time to add margin before forced liquidation. This finding lacks legal basis and constitutes an error in legal application. According to Article 10 of the Futures Brokerage Contract between the two parties, as long as the Tianjin Business Department issued a margin call notice to Fan Youfu as agreed, and Fan Youfu failed to timely add margin or immediately take measures to reduce positions before the market opened the next day, the Tianjin Business Department had the right to forcibly liquidate Fan Youfu's positions. However, the first-instance judgment stated: "The above contract did not stipulate a reasonable time for adding margin." This means the second-instance judgment did not recognize the agreement of the two parties in the above contract. (2) The basic facts found in the second-instance judgment are not supported by evidence. After the close of the previous day, the Tianjin Business Department issued a margin call notice to Fan Youfu, requiring him to add over RMB 13 million in margin before the opening of the market the next day. At the opening of the market the next day, Fan Youfu neither added margin nor gave any instruction to close positions on his own. The Tianjin Business Department forcibly liquidated 412 lots of some positions after the market opened. At 13:38 p.m., Fan Youfu added RMB 1.5 million to his account. In terms of both the time of receipt and the amount received, this was "unreasonable." Therefore, the finding in the second-instance judgment that the Tianjin Business Department was at fault is untenable. (3) The calculation of losses is erroneous. On December 25, 2007, Fan Youfu's "Transaction Settlement Statement" showed a profit/loss from position closing of over -RMB 13 million, which was the total profit/loss from the establishment to the closure of all Fan Youfu's closed positions. This was an investment loss caused by Fan Youfu's wrong direction of trading, not a loss caused by the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department. The Tianjin Business Department forcibly liquidated positions at 8:59 a.m. If Fan Youfu's funds had arrived before 9:30 a.m., Fan Youfu could have requested the Tianjin Business Department to immediately restore his positions or placed orders himself to restore positions. The difference between the forced liquidation and the re-establishment of positions would then be the actual loss caused to Fan Youfu by the "fault" of the Tianjin Business Department. Since Fan Youfu did not add margin within a "reasonable" time, there was no issue of restoring positions in his account, and the fault of the Tianjin Business Department had no corresponding consequences. Therefore, according to the liability found in the second-instance judgment, the fault of the Tianjin Business Department did not cause actual losses to Fan Youfu's account. In summary, the Tianjin Business Department requested the revocation of the second-instance judgment, a change in the judgment to dismiss all of Fan Youfu's claims, and that Fan Youfu bear all litigation costs.

The respondent Fan Youfu argued in defense: (1) The second-instance judgment has a legal basis and should be upheld in accordance with the law. (2) The Tianjin Business Department's application for retrial does not conform to the facts, evidence, and law and should be dismissed in accordance with the law. First, the Tianjin Business Department's unilateral substantial increase in margin ratios lacks a basis, and its notice to Fan Youfu to add margin was unreasonably timed. Second, the Tianjin Business Department's forced liquidation timing was unreasonable and violated regulations, depriving the respondent of the right to reduce positions on his own. Its liquidation actions were not only excessive in quantity but also inconsistent with practices and regulations in liquidation order. (3) The black-box operations commonly used by the Tianjin Business Department should be thoroughly investigated in accordance with the law. The respondent requested the dismissal of the retrial application and the upholding of the original second-instance judgment.

During the retrial, this Court further found the following: On December 21, 2007 (Friday), the margin ratios for Shanghai Futures Exchange contracts Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 were all 7%; the margin ratio of the Tianjin Business Department was 9.5% for all. On December 24, Cu0802 contract experienced its first daily price limit up, Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts experienced their second daily price limit up. After the close that day, the Shanghai Futures Exchange issued an announcement stating: Today, Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts experienced their second daily price limit up. According to trading rules, the price fluctuation range for the next trading day for the above contracts shall be adjusted to 6%, and the trading margin ratio shall be adjusted to 9%; Cu0802 contract experienced its first daily price limit up, and the price fluctuation range for the next trading day for the above contract shall be adjusted to 5%, with the trading margin ratio remaining at 7%. Accordingly, after the close on the 24th, the Tianjin Business Department adjusted the margin ratio for Cu0802 contract to 14.5%, and for Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts to 16.5%. After the close on the 25th, Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts did not experience a third daily price limit up, and the Shanghai Futures Exchange adjusted the margin ratio for these two contracts to 6.5%; Cu0802 contract did not experience a second daily price limit up, and the Shanghai Futures Exchange kept the margin ratio for this contract at 7%. The Tianjin Business Department then adjusted the margin ratios for Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts to 9%, and for Cu0802 contract to 9.5%.

The times and prices at which Fan Youfu opened short positions in Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 contracts, and the closing prices of the contracts on the respective days, are as follows:
Cu0802 contract: On December 20, 2007, opened 33 lots with an average opening price of RMB 55,659.09; the closing price that day was RMB 56,020.
Cu0803 contract: On November 23 of the same year, opened 15 lots with an average opening price of RMB 54,412.67; the closing price that day was RMB 55,500; on November 26, opened 22 lots with an average opening price of RMB 55,369.09; the closing price that day was RMB 54,620; on November 27, opened 35 lots with an average opening price of RMB 54,051.43; the closing price that day was RMB 54,300; on November 28, opened 22 lots with an average opening price of RMB 54,533.18; the closing price that day was RMB 55,500; on November 29, opened 25 lots with an average opening price of RMB 56,467.60; the closing price that day was RMB 57,040; on November 30, opened 4 lots with an average opening price of RMB 56,965.00; the closing price that day was RMB 57,880; on December 4, opened 60 lots with an average opening price of RMB 55,913.50; the closing price that day was RMB 55,690; on December 5, opened 50 lots with an average opening price of RMB 55,428.40; the closing price that day was RMB 56,930; on December 6, opened 31 lots with an average opening price of RMB 56,577.74; the closing price that day was RMB 56,300; on December 10, opened 19 lots with an average opening price of RMB 56,774.20; the closing price that day was RMB 56,900; on December 14, opened 5 lots with an average opening price of RMB 53,820.00; the closing price that day was RMB 54,120; on December 17, opened 8 lots with an average opening price of RMB 54,345.00; the closing price that day was RMB 53,950; on December 18, opened 73 lots with an average opening price of RMB 52,641.92; the closing price that day was RMB 52,410.
Cu0804 contract: On December 13, opened 9 lots with an average opening price of RMB 54,628.89; the closing price that day was RMB 54,990; on December 17, opened 1 lot with an opening price of RMB 54,850.00; the closing price that day was RMB 54,000.
Based on the above, the average selling prices of Fan Youfu's short positions opened were: 33 lots Cu0802 at RMB 55,659.09; 369 lots Cu0803 at RMB 54,860.78; 10 lots Cu0804 at RMB 54,651.

The transaction settlement statement for Fan Youfu dated December 24 provided by the Tianjin Business Department showed: "Current balance: RMB 15,342,772.36; Floating profit/loss: -RMB 7,733,100.00; Client equity: RMB 7,609,672.36; Margin used: RMB 20,968,191.75; Available funds: -RMB 13,358,519.39; Risk ratio: 36.29%; Margin call: RMB 13,358,519.39. The settlement prices for the three contracts Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 on the 24th were: RMB 59,690, RMB 58,330, and RMB 58,630, respectively." This transaction settlement statement was calculated by the Tianjin Business Department after the close on the 24th, based on the adjusted margin ratios for the next trading day: 14.5% for Cu0802 and 16.5% for Cu0803 and Cu0804. If the margin ratios on the 24th had all been calculated at 9.5%, then the current balance in Fan Youfu's fund account would have been RMB 24,124,957.86; the floating profit/loss would be -RMB 7,733,100.00; client equity would be RMB 16,391,857.86; margin used would be RMB 12,186,006.25; and the risk ratio would be 74.34%.

At 8:55 a.m. on December 25, the Tianjin Business Department placed orders to forcibly liquidate Fan Youfu's 412 lots of short positions at the daily price limit up price. For the Cu0802 contract, this was the second daily price limit up; for Cu0803 and Cu0804 contracts, this was the third daily price limit up. During the call auction, all 412 lots of the three contracts were executed at non-limited-up prices, and the execution prices were those found in the first-instance trial. The Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 contracts expired on February 15, March 15, and April 15, 2008, respectively, with delivery prices of RMB 63,660, RMB 66,810, and RMB 64,200.

Article 28 of the futures brokerage contract signed between Fan Youfu and the Tianjin Business Department stipulates: "If the futures company's forced liquidation does not meet the agreed conditions, the Tianjin Business Department shall restore the forcibly liquidated positions and compensate for the direct losses caused thereby."

This Court, upon retrial, holds that the futures brokerage contract signed between the parties in this case contains risk control provisions in Articles 6, 7, 10, 11, and 14 regarding margin ratios and additions, as well as conditions for implementing forced liquidation. At the same time, Article 29 and Article 38 of the State Council's "Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading," and Article 36 and Article 40 of this Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Futures Dispute Cases" clearly stipulate the maintenance margin standards and legal and contractual forced liquidation. Therefore, the civil damages lawsuit filed by Fan Youfu, based on the contract between the parties and legal provisions such as the "Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading," alleging that the Tianjin Business Department's forced liquidation was improper and infringed on his lawful rights and interests, is a lawsuit involving the concurrence of contractual liability and tort liability. The focus of dispute between the parties in this case is whether the Tianjin Business Department was at fault in the forced liquidation and whether it should bear civil liability, the composition of Fan Youfu's losses, and the scope of the Tianjin Business Department's liability.

(1) Whether the Tianjin Business Department was at fault in the forced liquidation and whether it should bear civil liability.

Forced liquidation is a measure provided by law and contract. When a client's account margin is insufficient and the client fails to add margin as required and also fails to close positions on their own, the futures company has the right, for risk control purposes, to take positions opposite to the client's existing positions to close out the client's positions in a certain financial asset. For the client, forced liquidation is the most stringent risk control measure implemented by another party after the client's futures trading losses reach a certain level. Therefore, the provision in Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading" that "when the client's margin is insufficient, the client shall timely add margin or close positions on its own. If the client fails to timely add margin or close positions on its own within the time limit prescribed by the futures company, the futures company shall forcibly liquidate the client's contracts, and the relevant expenses and losses incurred from the forced liquidation shall be borne by the client" sets forth three conditions before the futures company can take forced liquidation measures: First, the client's margin is insufficient; second, the client has not added margin as required in a timely manner; and third, the client has not timely closed positions on its own. Only when the above three legal conditions are satisfied does the futures company have the right to forcibly liquidate. If the futures company does not strictly comply with legal provisions and contractual agreements when executing forced liquidation, this will cause the client not only to bear the potential damages from market trading risks but also to bear the damages from human risks in the market operation mechanism.

(1) Whether there was fault in the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department and whether it damaged Fan Youfu's rights and interests should be analyzed based on the three conditions stated above. First, whether Fan Youfu's margin was insufficient. After the close of trading on Monday, December 24, 2007, the Shanghai Futures Exchange adjusted the margin ratio for Cu0803 and Cu0804 to 9% and for Cu0802 to 7% for the next trading day. The Tianjin Business Department correspondingly and substantially increased the margin ratio for Cu0803 and Cu0804 to 16.5% and for Cu0802 to 14.5% for the next trading day. Because the Shanghai Futures Exchange and the Tianjin Business Department adjusted the margin ratio for the 25th after the close of trading on the 24th, the settlement on the 24th itself should still have been executed according to the margin ratio of the 21st (Friday). On the 21st, the margin ratios for Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 contracts at the Shanghai Futures Exchange were all 7%; the margin ratios for these three contracts at the Tianjin Business Department were all 9.5%. The trading settlement statement for the 24th submitted by the Tianjin Business Department in the litigation was, however, executed using the substantially increased margin ratios of 16.5% and 14.5% for the 25th. If the data on this trading settlement statement were true, the Tianjin Business Department should not have waited until the 25th to take forced liquidation measures; it should have forced liquidation during the trading session on the 24th. Because, based on the data on that settlement statement, the risk ratio calculated from margin occupation / customer equity would not be 36.29% as shown on the statement, but 275.54%. A risk ratio of 275.54% means that not only was all of Fan Youfu's margin occupied by the held contracts, but the Tianjin Business Department had also paid 175.54% of the funds occupied by the contracts for him. Therefore, the trading settlement statement submitted by the Tianjin Business Department, which was calculated based on the margin ratio of the 25th, cannot prove that Fan Youfu's margin was insufficient in the settlement on the 24th. This method of settlement, using the margin ratio of the next trading day as the basis for that day's settlement, is contrary to the trading rules of the Shanghai Futures Exchange, and thus this Court does not accept it. If the margin ratio was calculated at 9.5%, after the close of trading on the 24th, Fan Youfu's account customer equity was RMB 16,391,857.86, margin occupation was RMB 12,186,006.25, the risk ratio was 74.34%, and the available funds were positive. Therefore, this Court supports Fan Youfu's defense that on the 24th, following the notice from the Tianjin Business Department, he voluntarily closed 270 lots of soybean contracts, bringing his account into compliance with the Tianjin Business Department's margin ratio requirement for that day. If Fan Youfu continued to hold the positions without adding margin, even if the margin ratio was not increased, as contract prices fluctuated, his account might still incur a deficit in the future. Nevertheless, it is not permissible to determine that Fan Youfu's account had insufficient margin on the 24th based on facts that have not yet occurred. Second, whether Fan Youfu timely added margin as required. First, the risk ratio, also known as the risk degree, is a risk control parameter calculated by dividing the margin occupied by contracts in a futures trading customer's account by the customer's equity. The lower the risk ratio, the more available funds the customer has, the less margin is occupied by contracts, and the lower the margin risk. Standard futures brokerage contracts generally stipulate that if the risk ratio is greater than 100%, meaning the available funds in the customer's account are less than zero, the futures company shall, during the trading session or at settlement, issue a notice to the customer restricting the opening of new positions, requiring additional margin, or requiring voluntary liquidation. The customer shall timely add margin or voluntarily close positions during the trading session to bring the risk ratio below 100%, meaning the available funds in the account are greater than zero. Otherwise, the futures company has the right to forcibly liquidate some or all of the customer's held positions until the customer's available funds are greater than zero, i.e., the risk ratio is below 100%. However, Article 10 of the futures brokerage contract in this case stipulates that when the risk ratio was below 100%, the Tianjin Business Department could issue a notice to Fan Youfu restricting the opening of new positions, requiring additional margin, or requiring voluntary liquidation. Fan Youfu was then required to timely add margin or immediately take steps to reduce positions. Otherwise, the Tianjin Business Department had the right, without prior notice to Fan Youfu, to forcibly liquidate some or all of Fan Youfu's open positions. Obviously, the content of this clause is inconsistent with the connotation of risk ratio parameter setting, the purpose and method of margin risk control. Replacing the condition of "greater than 100%" with "less than 100%" means that the Tianjin Business Department could, at any time, take measures such as restricting the opening of new positions, notifying for additional margin and voluntary liquidation, and if requirements were not met, proceed to forced liquidation. Second, the law and the contract stipulate that when a customer's margin is insufficient, it shall be timely added. However, "timely" is based on the premise that addition is possible. After the close of trading on the 24th, based on the substantially increased margin ratio, Fan Youfu's account faced insufficient margin requiring addition for the 25th. Yet the Tianjin Business Department did not notify Fan Youfu of the increased margin ratio until 18:50 that evening, demanding an additional margin of RMB 13.36 million before the market opened on the 25th, or else forced liquidation would occur. However, from 18:50 that evening to 9:00 the next morning, banks and other financial institutions were closed for business. During this period, Fan Youfu had no possibility of adding margin. Before 9:00 on the 25th, during the call auction period of the futures market, the Tianjin Business Department forcibly liquidated 412 lots of Fan Youfu's short contracts at the third and second limit-up prices, and all were executed at non-limit-up prices. Therefore, the fact that Fan Youfu did not add margin should be characterized as the Tianjin Business Department failing to give Fan Youfu an opportunity to add margin, rather than Fan Youfu failing to meet the requirement or lacking the ability to add margin. Third, whether the margin ratio applied by the Tianjin Business Department on the 25th was reasonable. The level of the margin ratio directly affects the amount of funds occupied in futures trading and settlement, and directly affects the level of risk for customers in futures trading settlement. The law stipulates that the margin collected by a futures company from a customer shall not be lower than the standard set by the futures exchange, but does not specify how much higher it may be. On December 21, the margin ratio of the Tianjin Business Department was not more than 3% higher than that of the Shanghai Futures Exchange. However, after the close of trading on the 24th, the Tianjin Business Department substantially increased the standard, with the margin ratios for three contracts all exceeding the Shanghai Futures Exchange standard by 7.5 percentage points. At the close of trading on the 25th, the Shanghai Futures Exchange did not adjust the margin ratio, but the Tianjin Business Department itself reduced the margin ratios for these three contracts back to 9.5% and 9% respectively. Thus, the change in the margin ratio by the Tianjin Business Department on the 25th was arbitrary and sudden. Although the contract in this case did not clearly specify how much higher the margin ratio could be than the Shanghai Futures Exchange standard, based on the content of the agreement between the parties, "the [Business Department] may at any time notify the margin ratio on its own, and may at any time increase the margin ratio solely for Fan Youfu," the Tianjin Business Department's arbitrary and substantial single-day increase in the margin ratio for Fan Youfu may not appear to be a breach of contract. However, in the highly risky futures market, such arbitrary behavior of substantially increasing the margin ratio for a single day, far exceeding the futures exchange standard, objectively subjects the customer not only to the trading risks of the futures market but also to man-made risks arising from the operating mechanism beyond the market trading risks. The clause "may at any time notify the margin ratio on its own, and may at any time increase the margin ratio solely for Fan Youfu" is a general clause presented in a standard form contract. When different understandings arise in the performance of a standard form contract, or when an unfair situation occurs in its performance, Article 41 of the Contract Law of the PRC shall apply, and the contract shall be interpreted and determined in favor of the party that did not provide the standard form contract (the customer). Therefore, the act of implementing a margin ratio increase far exceeding the Shanghai Futures Exchange standard solely for Fan Youfu for just one trading day, the 25th, was unfair and unreasonable. Fourth, whether Fan Youfu had a timely opportunity to voluntarily close positions. The law does not specify how long a period before forced liquidation constitutes "timely" for voluntary liquidation. However, practical reality requires that voluntary liquidation must occur during the futures trading hours. If the market is not open on that day, requiring the customer to close positions or place closing orders constitutes a distorted interpretation of the legally prescribed timely voluntary liquidation operation, and is an overly harsh requirement on the customer. During the call auction period on the 25th before the market opened, Fan Youfu's 412 lots of contracts were forcibly liquidated. The Tianjin Business Department not only failed to give Fan Youfu an opportunity to add margin, but also did not even give him an opportunity to voluntarily close positions.

Based on the timing, price, and quantity of the forced liquidation in this case, combined with the substantial single-day increase in the margin ratio, it can be determined that the Tianjin Business Department did not act in good faith, and the forced liquidation implemented without satisfying the conditions stipulated by law and the contract was faulty. According to Article 28 of the contract between the parties, "If the futures company's forced liquidation does not meet the agreed conditions, the Tianjin Business Department shall restore the liquidated positions and compensate for the direct losses caused thereby," and according to Article 40 of this Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Futures Disputes, "If a futures exchange, in violation of the trading rules of the futures exchange or the conditions, timing, or method for forced liquidation agreed in the futures brokerage contract, causes losses to a futures company or customer, the futures exchange or futures company shall bear liability for compensation," the Tianjin Business Department shall bear civil liability for the losses caused to Fan Youfu by its forced liquidation. This Court does not support the Tianjin Business Department's retrial argument that it had the right to forcibly liquidate Fan Youfu's held positions because Fan Youfu neither added margin nor gave instructions for voluntary liquidation. Fan Youfu's defense argument that the Tianjin Business Department's timing requirements for margin addition and forced liquidation were unreasonable and violated regulations, depriving him of the right to voluntarily reduce positions, is established, and this Court supports it.

(2) Concerning the composition of Fan Youfu's losses and the scope of liability of the Tianjin Business Department.

Risks in the futures market include both market trading risks and market operation risks. Market trading risks are legally borne by the futures trader, whereas market operation risks are not legally borne by the futures trader. If losses or risks to a futures trader are caused by man-made errors in the market operation mechanism, the responsible party shall bear liability. Futures trading risks mainly arise from the trader's incorrect judgment of contract price trends and contract price fluctuations, amplified by the margin trading system. Specifically in this case, from the time Fan Youfu opened short positions in the Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 contracts until they were forcibly liquidated, the total loss amounted to RMB 13,066,500, which includes both the losses caused by Fan Youfu's own incorrect judgment in futures trading and the increased losses due to the fault of the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department — that is, the futures trading losses and the forced liquidation losses. First, analysis of futures trading losses. Based on the timing and price at which Fan Youfu opened short positions in the Cu0802, Cu0803, and Cu0804 contracts, the overall price trend of these three contracts after the positions were opened, the delivery prices of the three contracts at expiration, and the daily trading settlement statements, it is proven that Fan Youfu made a fundamental error in judging the price trend of the three contracts. Fan Youfu opened short positions when the prices of the three contracts were relatively low, and continued to hold these positions as the prices trended higher with fluctuations. This was the fundamental cause of Fan Youfu's futures trading losses in this case. Pursuant to the daily mark-to-market settlement system implemented in futures trading, cumulative settlement up to the close of trading on the 24th showed a floating loss of RMB 7,733,100 on Fan Youfu's trading settlement statement. This floating loss was entirely caused by Fan Youfu's incorrect judgment and continued holding of positions. In other words, as long as the prices of these three contracts did not fall below Fan Youfu's opening prices and Fan Youfu continued to hold the positions, he would always be in a floating loss state. During this period, no matter who closed the positions, the floating loss would become a realized loss. Therefore, as of the close of trading on the 24th, the cumulative settlement floating loss in Fan Youfu's futures trading was not triggered by the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department; that is, the conversion of the floating loss of over RMB 7.7 million into a realized loss had no direct causal relationship with the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department. Second, the liability method for faulty forced liquidation. If a futures company's forced liquidation is faulty and the act damages the customer's interests, thus requiring civil liability, according to the methods of assuming civil liability stipulated in Article 134 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the PRC, the futures company should take remedial measures to restore the customer's forcibly liquidated positions. If restoration of positions is impossible, the futures company shall compensate the customer for the resulting losses at a fair and reasonable price. Article 28 of the contract between the parties in this case also contains such a provision. Because the three contracts in this case have already expired and been delivered, restoring the forcibly liquidated positions has become impossible. Therefore, the Tianjin Business Department can only compensate Fan Youfu for the losses incurred due to the forced liquidation. Third, calculation of forced liquidation losses. From the perspective of the Tianjin Business Department, after the forced liquidation, the prices of the three contracts still trended higher with fluctuations, and the average of the daily settlement prices up to the delivery date, as well as the delivery prices of the three contracts, were all higher than the forced liquidation prices. From Fan Youfu's perspective, the closing prices of the three contracts on the 25th were lower than the closing prices on the 24th, and the closing prices on the 28th were even lower. If he had added margin or voluntarily closed positions, he could have reduced his losses further. Both parties' above views are based on assumptions and are taken from their own favorable perspectives, rather than correctly thinking and fairly recognizing the facts based on the forced liquidation that has already occurred. Moreover, the views of both parties do not conform to the characteristics of the futures market. In the futures market, anyone can make an accurate judgment about price movements that have already occurred and choose a favorable price for themselves. However, neither party can be absolutely certain of the accuracy of their forecast regarding future price movements that have not yet occurred. Therefore, based on the established fact of forced liquidation, the calculation benchmark for forced liquidation losses should be sought retrospectively, not prospectively, in order to be objective and fair. Accordingly, this Court does not accept or support the arguments of either party that favor themselves while ignoring the other party's interests. In summary, taking the facts of Fan Youfu's positions and the settlement data after the close of trading on the 24th as the benchmark to determine the scope of the Tianjin Business Department's fault liability is relatively objective and fair for both parties. Then, the difference between the account loss of RMB 13,066,500 after the forced liquidation on the 25th and the floating loss of RMB 7,733,100 after the close of trading on the 24th, which is RMB 5,333,400, represents the loss caused to Fan Youfu by the forced liquidation and is the scope of compensation the Tianjin Business Department should bear.

The judgments of the first instance and second instance in this case both correctly held that the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department was faulty and that it should bear corresponding liability towards Fan Youfu. However, the first instance judgment of the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court calculated the loss as RMB 6,663,000 based on the difference between the forced liquidation prices of the three contracts and the closing prices on the same day after liquidation. This calculation used the contract price at some point in time after the forced liquidation as a reference, making it difficult to be objective and fair. Furthermore, it differed from the price at the point in time argued by Fan Youfu and the Tianjin Business Department respectively, and both parties did not accept it. Not only did that court's loss calculation method fail to conform to the characteristics and rules of the futures market, but it also erroneously determined that the loss caused by the fault of the Tianjin Business Department in the forced liquidation resulted from mixed fault of both parties, ordering the Tianjin Business Department to bear 60% and Fan Youfu to bear 40%. Therefore, the first instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and improper allocation of responsibility. The second instance judgment of the Tianjin High People's Court relied entirely on Fan Youfu's claims, failing to separate Fan Youfu's trading losses caused by his incorrect judgment and continued holding of positions from the overall loss, and commingled them with the losses caused by the fault of the forced liquidation by the Tianjin Business Department. It ordered the Tianjin Business Department to bear all of Fan Youfu's losses of RMB 9,027,085.66, calculated based on the closing prices on the 28th. This was also partly unclear in fact-finding and improper in responsibility allocation. Therefore, this Court, in this retrial, corrects the judgments of the first and second instances in this case.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 186, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 38 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law in Retrial Procedures, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment No. 0028 (2009) Jin Gao Min Er Zhong Zi of the Tianjin High People's Court;

2. Set aside the Civil Judgment No. 61 (2008) Yi Zhong Min Er Chu Zi of the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court;

3. Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Business Department shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Fan Youfu for losses in the amount of RMB 5,333,400;

4. Dismiss Fan Youfu's other claims.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,989 and the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,989 shall be borne by Yinjian Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd., Tianjin Business Department.

This judgment is final.
